receipt_kinds.when_produced: Direct output of multi-segment execution; vector of SegmentReceipts (one STARK per segment via RISC-V circuit) plus optional assumption receipts; used when full segment details or assumptions are retained
After recursion (lift + join/resolve) aggregates a CompositeReceipt (or prior SuccinctReceipts) into a single STARK via the recursion circuit; constant-size independent of segment count
After STARK-to-SNARK compression: a SuccinctReceipt is verified inside the Groth16 circuit (identity_p254 + compress) producing a BN254 Groth16 proof; intended for on-chain / succinct verification
Dev-mode only; no cryptographic seal; for rapid prototyping

groth16_receipt_fields.type_shape: Vec<u8> (or structured a/b/c points after selector); typically 4-byte selector + Groth16 proof (A, B, C on BN254)
groth16_receipt_fields.meaning: The opaque Groth16 proof attesting that the recursion/identity circuit accepted the claim under the control root
groth16_receipt_fields.verifier_must_check: Parse selector, decode proof points, run pairing check against fixed verifying key with public inputs (split control_root, split claim_digest, bn254_control_id)
groth16_receipt_fields.failure_if_skipped: Arbitrary forged seal accepted; any claim/journal can be asserted without a valid proof

groth16_receipt_fields.meaning: The public statement being proven: pre/post system state, exit code, input digest, output (journal + assumptions)
groth16_receipt_fields.verifier_must_check: Recompute claim.digest() and ensure it matches the claim digest fed as public input to the Groth16 verifier; for ok() receipts also check exit_code == Halted(0) and journal matches
groth16_receipt_fields.failure_if_skipped: Journal/claim substitution: attacker supplies a valid seal for one claim but a different journal or image_id

groth16_receipt_fields.meaning: Fingerprint of the expected control_root, bn254_control_id and verifying_key; allows version detection without embedding full parameters
groth16_receipt_fields.verifier_must_check: Compare against the digest of the trusted parameters the verifier was compiled/configured with; reject mismatch
groth16_receipt_fields.failure_if_skipped: Cross-version confusion: a seal produced under an old/new control root or VK is accepted by a verifier expecting different parameters

components.pre: MaybePruned<SystemState> or Digest (image_id / pre-state merkle root + pc; for ok receipts often just the image_id)
components.post: MaybePruned<SystemState> (post-state pc + memory merkle root; often zeroed for Halted(0))
components.input: Digest (commitment to guest input; frequently zero)
components.output: MaybePruned<Output> where Output = { journal: Digest (SHA-256 of journal bytes), assumptions: Digest }

claim_structure.claim_digest_computation: Tagged structural hash (sha256 of tag 'risc0.ReceiptClaim' || input || pre || post.digest() || output.digest() || exit_code packing || length); exact byte layout is version-stable within a major release but uses the risc0 tagged-struct encoding. For the common 'ok' case: ReceiptClaim::ok(image_id, journal_digest) produces a claim whose digest is the value placed in Groth16 public inputs.

binding_chain: claim_digest is split into two 128-bit limbs (byte-reversed) and supplied as public inputs to the Groth16 circuit together with the two limbs of control_root and the bn254_control_id
Groth16 seal is a proof that the recursion/identity circuit accepted exactly those public inputs under the verifying key

control_root (Merkle root of allowed recursion control IDs) and verifying_key are fixed parameters of the verifier; they bind the seal to a specific circuit version; bn254_control_id identifies the Poseidon-BN254 control program used in the final recursion step

circuit_version_dependent: control_root (and the set of control IDs it commits to)
selector (first 4 bytes of seal, derived from parameters)
exact tagged-hash encoding of ReceiptClaim / SystemState / Output (minor layout changes across major releases)
version_coupling.what_breaks_wrong_version: Pairing check fails (wrong VK), or selector mismatch aborts early, or claim_digest computed with different tagging does not match the public input the seal was generated for; a verifier that ignores the parameters digest can accept a seal from an incompatible recursion circuit that proves a different statement

common_verifier_bugs.bug: Accepting seal without checking claim_digest == public-input claim limbs
common_verifier_bugs.check_that_catches_it: Recompute claim.digest() from the supplied ReceiptClaim / journal and compare to the value reconstructed from the Groth16 public signals

common_verifier_bugs.bug: Ignoring exit_code / treating any Halted(n) as success
common_verifier_bugs.check_that_catches_it: Explicitly require ExitCode::Halted(0) (or the application-specific success code) after claim decoding

common_verifier_bugs.bug: Not verifying journal bytes hash to the journal_digest inside the claim
Using a hard-coded or wrong control_root / VK for the seal's selector
common_verifier_bugs.check_that_catches_it: Selector match + parameters-digest equality against the trusted Groth16ReceiptVerifierParameters

common_verifier_bugs.bug: Treating MaybePruned::Pruned values as trusted without the seal binding them
common_verifier_bugs.check_that_catches_it: Only accept pruned fields when the claim_digest (which includes those digests) has been verified by the seal

common_verifier_bugs.bug: Forgetting to reject non-empty assumptions on an unconditional receipt
common_verifier_bugs.check_that_catches_it: Assert assumptions digest is zero (or explicitly resolve every assumption) when the receipt is presented as unconditional

certainty_notes.receipt_kinds: High — directly from official docs and source (Composite / Succinct / Groth16 / Fake)
certainty_notes.groth16_receipt_fields: High for field names and roles (seal, claim, verifier_parameters) from risc0-zkvm source and ethereum verifier contracts; exact seal byte layout (selector + a/b/c) confirmed by on-chain verifier
certainty_notes.claim_structure: High for the logical components (pre/post/exit/input/output/journal); medium on the precise tagged-hash byte ordering (known to be 'risc0.ReceiptClaim' tagged struct but exact field order/packing taken from Solidity helper and Rust Digestible impls)
certainty_notes.binding_chain: High — public-input construction (split digests of control_root + claim + bn254_control_id) is explicit in the Groth16 verifier contract and Rust verification path
certainty_notes.version_coupling: High — selector and parameters digest exist precisely to detect version skew; control_root / VK are the classic circuit-version parameters
certainty_notes.common_verifier_bugs: Medium-high — derived from the checks that the reference verifiers perform and from observed failure modes (ClaimDigestMismatch, SelectorMismatch, exit-code handling); not an exhaustive CVE list
